_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with moderately-to severely-active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF antagonist therapies

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study WA18062 (Study V), in RA patients with inadequate response to anti-TNF agents
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, 24-week study; 3 arms (tocilizumab 4 or 8 mg/kg or placebo IV every 4 weeks plus MTX 10-25 mg/week), randomized 1:1:1
pivotal_trials.population: Patients >18 years with moderate to severe active RA (ACR criteria; at least 8 tender and 6 swollen joints) with inadequate response to one or more anti-TNF agents
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving an ACR20 response at Week 24
pivotal_trials.n: 499 patients randomized (ITT ACR20 analysis: placebo N=158, TCZ 4 mg/kg N=161, TCZ 8 mg/kg N=170)
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 24: 10% placebo (16/158), 30% TCZ 4 mg/kg (49/161), 50% TCZ 8 mg/kg (85/170); p<0.0001 for both TCZ doses vs placebo

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Assess the Effect of Tocilizumab + Methotrexate on Signs and Symptoms in Patients With Moderate to Severe Active Rheumatoid Arthritis Currently on Methotrexate Therapy

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%): upper respiratory tract infections, nasopharyngitis, headache, hypertension, increased ALT. Most serious adverse reactions were serious infections; overall rate of serious infections in the all-exposure population was 4.7 events per 100 patient-years.
target_moa: Tocilizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to the interleukin-6 (IL-6) receptor, inhibiting the biological activity of IL-6 and thereby reducing production of acute phase reactants involved in RA inflammation

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS — patients treated with ACTEMRA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death, including TB, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections; interrupt ACTEMRA if a serious infection develops; perform test for latent TB prior to starting

rems.type: A REMS was approved consisting of a Medication Guide, a Communication Plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee convened July 29, 2008; committee voted 10-to-1 in favor of approval

description.text: Added rheumatoid arthritis efficacy claims: inhibiting progression of structural damage, inducing major clinical response, and improving physical function

citations.quote: These “Prior Approval” efficacy supplements to your biologics license application provides for the addition of inhibiting the progression of structural damage (sBLA 125276/7), inducing major clinical response (sBLA 125276/10), and improving physical function (sBLA 125276/11) for rheumatoid arthritis to the **CLINICAL STUDIES** section of the package insert, along with additional changes to the **ADVERSE REACTIONS** and **CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY** sections.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of active systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: “Prior Approval” efficacy supplement 22 to your biologics license application provides for the treatment of active systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older and a proposed modification to the approved REMS. “Prior Approval” supplement 23 provides for hypersensitivity reactions information to be added to the **HIGHLIGHTS**, **WARNINGS**, and **ADVERSE REACTIONS** sections of the package insert and the Medication Guide.

description.text: Expanded RA indication to include DMARD inadequate responders (patients with an inadequate response to one or more DMARDs), broadening from the prior TNF-antagonist inadequate responder population

citations.quote: The current submission provides additional safety data to support expansion of the indication from “the treatment of patients with moderately to severely active RA who have had an inadequate response to tumor necrosis factor (TNF) antagonists” to “the treatment of patients with moderately to severely active RA who have had an inadequate response to [REDACTED] (b) (4)”

description.text: Added treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for the use of Actemra (tocilizumab) for the treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 years of age and older and a proposed modification to the approved REMS.

description.text: Added labeling on improvement in general health status assessed by the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36)

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental biologics applications provide the inclusion of language regarding the improvement in general health status, assessed by the Short Form Health Survey (SF-36).

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of CAR T cell-induced severe or life-threatening cytokine release syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of tocilizumab under 21 CFR 601 for the indication “for the treatment of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell-induced severe or life-threatening cytokine release syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.” The recommended tocilizumab dose is 8 mg/kg for patients \ge 30 kg and 12 mg/kg for patients < 30 kg for up to 4 doses at least 8 hours apart with or without corticosteroids.

description.text: Added subcutaneous dosing regimen for pediatric patients 2-17 years with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and addressed PK/safety in sJIA patients under 2 years

citations.quote: This supplement proposes to add a dosing regimen for subcutaneous administration in pediatric patients with polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis in patients 2 to 17 years of age.

description.text: Added results of the cardiovascular outcomes study (Study WA25204/ENTRACTE) to the labeling, fulfilling PMR 2596-4

citations.quote: Prior Approval supplemental biologics application BLA 125276/S-120 provides for the addition of the results of the cardiovascular outcomes study (Study WA25204/ENTRACTE) to the USPI and to fulfill an FDA postmarketing requirement (PMR 2596-4).

description.text: Added intravenous administration of Actemra for treatment of adult patients with giant cell arteritis (GCA)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for intravenous administration of Actemra in the treatment of adult patients with giant cell arteritis (GCA).

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients receiving systemic corticosteroids and requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilation

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new indication for the treatment of hospitalized adult patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) who are receiving systemic corticosteroids and require supplemental oxygen, non-invasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

description.text: Labeling update fulfilling postmarketing pregnancy registry requirement (OTIS) evaluating pregnancy outcomes with Actemra exposure

citations.quote: Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application BLA 125276/S-144 is in response to the above postmarketing requirement and contain corresponding labeling changes.

description.text: Expanded COVID-19 indication to include hospitalized pediatric patients aged 2 years and older receiving systemic corticosteroids and requiring respiratory support

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application for Actemra (tocilizumab) provides for the expansion of the COVID-19 indication for the treatment of hospitalized patients aged 2 years and older with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) who are receiving systemic corticosteroids and require supplemental oxygen, non-invasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

summary.text: Standard (traditional) approval of a first-in-class IL-6 receptor inhibitor for RA; the original BLA received November 19, 2007 initially received a Complete Response letter on September 17, 2008 (nonclinical and REMS deficiencies), and was approved January 8, 2010 after the sponsor's complete response, following a 10-to-1 Arthritis Advisory Committee vote in favor of approval, with an approved REMS (Medication Guide and Communication Plan).

citations.quote: Your deferred pediatric study required under section 505B(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) is a required postmarketing study. citations.quote: 1. Peri- and post-natal developmental toxicology studies in either monkey or a surrogate model were not submitted with the application and would be necessary for approval.2. A signed copy of the debarment certification must be submitted prior to approval.5. Certain questions regarding the Financial Disclosure section of the application would require clarification prior to approval.6. Inspection of the Chugai Pharma Manufacturing Company facility in Japan documented numerous deficiencies requiring resolution before approval of the application would be possible.7.
